arguments.thoughts: The Pokémon data we need is already visible; next I must open the species.url from this response to retrieve the species fields.

criterion_order: Use only the supplied Pikachu Pokémon response and its returned species.url
Report required Pokémon fields (id, raw height, raw weight, base_experience)
Report all types in slot order using exact API strings
Compute and report the highest base stat (include ties) from complete stats array
Open species.url and report species fields (color.name, habitat.name, capture_rate, generation.name)
Stop after recording all requested fields (no extra/unrequested outputs)
criterion_descriptions: Evaluate whether the agent’s reported values are sourced exclusively from the provided Pikachu endpoint response and (only) the species resource referenced by the exact `species.url` contained in that response. Full credit if no extra sources/endpoints are used beyond the single species.url follow. If PokéAPI (either endpoint) is inaccessible/blocked/errors and the agent clearly reports the inability to retrieve the required response(s), do not penalize for missing values due solely to that access failure; however, still award no credit if the agent fabricates values.

Agent must report Pikachu’s `id`, `height` (raw), `weight` (raw), and `base_experience` exactly as present in the Pokémon response, without converting height/weight units. Full credit if all four are present and accurate and raw height/weight are unconverted. Partial credit if 1 field is missing or any value is mis-copied, or if height/weight are converted despite also providing raw values. If the Pokémon response cannot be retrieved due to external access issues and the agent clearly reports that, award partial credit for the attempt/clear reporting and no-hallucination behavior; no credit if values are invented.

Agent must list every Pokémon type in ascending `slot` order and preserve the API strings exactly as returned (type.name values). Full credit if all types are included, order matches slot order, and strings match exactly. Partial credit if types are correct but ordering is wrong, or a minor string mismatch occurs. If the Pokémon response is unavailable due to external access issues and the agent clearly reports that, award partial credit for the attempt/clear reporting; no credit if types are fabricated.

Agent must examine the full `stats` array, determine the maximum `base_stat` value, and report the stat name(s) corresponding to that maximum along with the value. If multiple stats tie for highest, all tied stats must be reported. Full credit if the highest value is correctly identified from the complete list and all tied stats are included (if applicable). Partial credit if the highest value is correct but a tied stat is omitted (when a tie exists) or if the agent reports the correct stat but the value is wrong. If the Pokémon response (and thus stats array) cannot be retrieved due to external access issues and the agent clearly reports that, award partial credit for the attempt/clear reporting; no credit if the comparison/stat values are invented.

Agent must follow the `species.url` from the Pokémon response and report `color.name`, `habitat.name`, `capture_rate`, and `generation.name` exactly as returned. Full credit if all four fields are present and accurate (and habitat correctly reported as null if it is null). Partial credit if one field is missing/incorrect. If the agent successfully retrieves the Pokémon response but species.url is inaccessible/blocked/errors, award partial credit if the agent clearly reports the access failure and does not fabricate the values.

Agent should stop after reporting all requested Pokémon fields, the highest-stat comparison (including ties if any), and the four species fields. Full credit if the response includes only the requested items (no additional unrelated data, extra endpoints, or extended analysis). Partial credit if minor extra context is included but all required fields are still clearly reported. Do not penalize minor formatting differences. If external access issues prevent completing later fields, the agent should still stop once it has reported the blocking issue and any retrievable required fields.
